2026-09-25T02:36:26.0389729Z **Creating a Pull Request**
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0390065Z 
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0390297Z To create a pull request:
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0390929Z 1. Make any file changes directly in the working directory.
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0392141Z 2. If you haven't done so already, create a new local branch using `git checkout -b <branch-name>` with an appropriate unique name.
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0394187Z 3. Add and commit your changes to the branch. Be careful to add exactly the files you intend, and check there are no extra files left un-added. Verify you haven't deleted or changed any files you didn't intend to.
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0395832Z 4. Do not push your changes. That will be done by the tool.
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0397255Z 5. Create the pull request with the create_pull_request tool from safeoutputs exactly once, only when the final title/body/branch are ready.
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0399079Z 6. After calling `create_pull_request`, STOP. Do not probe with another PR call, do not test auth with manual `git push`, and do not rewrite git remotes.
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0400092Z 
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0402690Z **Important**: The `branch` parameter in the create_pull_request tool **must exactly match the name of your current local git branch** — the branch you just committed to. You can verify this with `git branch --show-current`. Never invent or guess a branch name; always use the actual branch name from `git branch --show-current`. If you are on an existing branch (e.g. you checked out a PR branch), use that branch name.
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0405180Z 
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0406952Z **Important**: `create_pull_request` is not a sandbox. Every successful call records a real PR intent that can become an externally visible pull request. 2026-09-25T02:36:26.0418252Z 
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0419493Z For `safeoutputs`, every successful call is a real write-intent declaration - do not use it for probing, auth checks, or placeholder payloads. Use `noop` or `report_incomplete` if not ready to emit the final action.
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0421046Z 
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0422210Z For multiple or complex arguments, pass the JSON object inline as a single quoted argument — the binary comes first, so a malformed command still runs the CLI and reports an error:
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0445663Z ```bash
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0446417Z safeoutputs add_comment '{"item_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody."}'
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0447475Z ```
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0448463Z Alternatively, pipe a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel (prefer this only for large bodies built from files):
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0449506Z ```bash
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0450172Z printf '{"item_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody."}' | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0451186Z # or read from a file: safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0451958Z ```
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0453169Z When piping, make sure the `|` is actually present: `printf '{...}' safeoutputs add_comment .` (no pipe) prints the JSON and exits 0 without ever running the CLI, so nothing is emitted.
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0454367Z 
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0457919Z **Multi-line or long `body` content:** do NOT build the JSON payload with `printf`/`echo` embedding raw newlines or many escaped characters directly in the command line — the sandbox's shell command-injection guard may reject long or complex quoted arguments (reporting "expansion patterns"/"command substitution" even though none are present) and retrying the identical command will fail again. Instead, write the content to a temp file with a heredoc, then use `jq -Rs` to inject it as the `body` field:
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0461194Z ```bash
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0461645Z cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/gh-aw/body.md
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0462183Z Title
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0462426Z 
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0462650Z Multi-line body content goes here.
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0463207Z EOF
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0463881Z jq -Rs '{title: "My title", body: .}' /tmp/gh-aw/body.md | safeoutputs create_discussion .
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0464702Z ```
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0465858Z If a shell command is rejected for containing expansion patterns, do not retry the same command — switch to the heredoc + `jq -Rs` pattern above.
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0466864Z 
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0467692Z To inject an entire local file as the `body` field without re-embedding its content in the model context, use `jq -Rs`:
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0468727Z ```bash
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0469243Z jq -Rs --arg discussion_number "$DISCUSSION_NUMBER" \
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0470046Z   '{discussion_number: ($discussion_number|tonumber), body: .}' \
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0470775Z   discussion-body.md \
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0471294Z   | safeoutputs update_discussion .
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0471842Z ```
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0473240Z `jq -Rs` reads the file as a raw string (`-R`) and slurps it into a single JSON string value (`-s`), so `body` is always a valid JSON field. Piping `cat file | safeoutputs ...` does not populate `body` and will be rejected.
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0474551Z 
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0475463Z The generated command syntax above is schema-derived from each enabled tool's final `inputSchema` and is the source of truth for required/optional parameters.
2026-09-25T02:36:26.0477639Z Use `<server> --help` and `<server> <tool> --help` for the same schema-derived signatures and examples before calling any command.
